sentences.text:
2. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Assistant Government Pleader for Home appearing for respondents.
3. Today, when the matter came up for hearing, learned Assistant Government Pleader for Home produced a copy of instructions of the Inspector of Police, Machilipatnam Rural Circle, wherein it is stated that, immediately upon receiving the complaint from the petitioner herein, they have registered the same as FIR in Crime No.33 of 2022 under Sections 420, 406 read with 34 IPC of Machilipatnam Police Station on 15.03.2022.
Thereafter, the Inspector of Chilakalapudi Police Station took up the investigation in the said case.

During the course of investigation, the Circle Inspector, Chilakalapudi examined LWs 1 to 14 and recorded their statements under Section 161(3)
Cr.P.C.,
However, the accused are still absconding, and their whereabouts have not been traced so far.
But, the Inspector of Police continues efforts to trace the whereabouts of the absconding accused, and then they will be apprehended and the case will be finalized as early as possible.

4. In view of the fact that the respondents have already examined LWs 1 to 14 and recorded their statements under Section 161(3) Cr.P.C., and are intending to apprehend the accused in the present case in order to proceed further in filing the charge sheet, instead of keeping the writ petition pending, this Court feels it appropriate to dispose of the writ petition by directing the respondent No.2 to file the charge sheet as expeditiously as possible, preferably within a period of eight (8)
weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
5. Accordingly, the Writ Petition is disposed of.
There shall be no order as to costs.
As a sequel, miscellaneous applications pending, if any, shall also stand closed.

__________________ JUSTICE V.SUJATHA KGR Silambarsan Panneerselvem vs The State Of Ap on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140807663/
